title: Study protocol bundle
description: The document that turns a generic Epidemica binary into a specific study. It names the modules the study uses and configures each of them, and it is the only artefact a researcher authors for a Tier 1 study: no application code is written, compiled or signed. The bundle is fetched after enrolment and verified against the `protocol_hash` returned there, and that hash is stamped on every observation so a dataset always says which configuration produced it.

bundle_version.description: Selects the bundle schema an app validates against. A binary that does not know this version must refuse the study rather than interpret it partially.

study_id.description: The study these observations belong to. Also the seed for the proximity service UUID, so devices in different studies never discover one another.

title.description: Shown to participants. This is the name a person sees when deciding whether they are in the right study.

description.description: Participant-facing explanation of what the study collects.

join_code.description: The code distributed to participants. Present so the authored bundle is self-describing; the app never reads it, having already used it to enrol.

modules.description: Module identifier to that module's configuration. Declaring a module and configuring it are the same act, so a bundle cannot name a module it forgot to configure, or configure one it never declared. An app that does not embed every module named here must refuse the study.

additionalProperties.description: Interpreted by the named module. Open by design: adding a module must not require a change to this schema.

sync.description: How eagerly the device tries to deliver what it has recorded.

min_interval_seconds.description: Lower bound between sync attempts. A floor rather than a schedule: the operating system decides when background work actually runs, and the exactly-once guarantees do not depend on it being punctual.

health.description: Whether devices report when their modules were actually collecting. On by default, because a study that cannot tell 'this participant met nobody' from 'we were not listening' has a defective dataset whether or not it notices. A study with no use for coverage can switch it off and save the observations.

interval_seconds.description: How often a device closes a coverage window. Shorter windows locate a gap more precisely and cost one observation per module per interval.

twin.description: A model the server runs against this study's data, whose output reaches participants through the state channel. Absent for studies that only collect: a study without this block is never simulated and never has participant state computed for it.

engine.description: Which runtime evaluates the model, e.g. `starsim`. A server that does not implement it must refuse the study rather than silently run nothing.

state_uri.description: Contract governing the state documents this model produces. What ties a twin to the state channel without either knowing about the other.

tick_interval_seconds.description: How often the model advances. Each tick is immutable once run, so this also sets how long a participant waits to learn what happened.

population.description: Total simulated population, enrolled participants included. Where it exceeds enrolment the remainder are virtual participants, whose presence the study must disclose.

pars.description: Engine-specific parameters, opaque to the platform. Interpreted only by the named engine.

rules.description: The scoring rules a study plays by, evaluated by the server and mirrored by the app for immediate feedback. Separate from `twin` because a model decides what happened to a participant and rules decide what it was worth; a study may have either without the other. Absent for studies that only collect.

engine.description: Which rule set applies, e.g. `epigame`. A server that does not implement it must refuse the study rather than silently score nothing.

pars.description: Every constant the rules use, so a second game with different economics needs no rebuild. Interpreted only by the named rule engine, and carried to the app unchanged so both sides score from one source.
